Selbach mac Ferchair was a key figure in 8th-century Irish politics, serving as king of the Cenél Loairn and of Dál Riata. His existence is well-documented in Irish annals, which frequently mention him as a prominent leader. The significance of Selbach mac Ferchair lies in his ability to unite disparate Irish kingdoms, fostering a period of relative peace and stability. This, in turn, allowed for the development of trade and cultural exchange between Ireland and other regions of Europe. The legacy of Selbach mac Ferchair can be seen in the continued influence of Dál Riata on Irish and Scottish history. He is also notable for his role in the early Christianization of Ireland, with many of the church's earliest structures and artifacts bearing his name. Selbach mac Ferchair's existence is a testament to the complex and often contentious nature of Irish politics during the medieval period. His reign marked a pivotal moment in Irish history, one that would shape the course of the country's development for centuries to come.

Selbach mac Ferchair's reign was marked by several significant events, including the construction of several important churches and the establishment of trade relationships with neighboring kingdoms. His military campaigns also expanded Dál Riata's borders, securing key territories and resources for the kingdom. The impact of Selbach mac Ferchair's reign can be seen in the many archaeological sites and historical records that remain today.

The legacy of Selbach mac Ferchair extends beyond his own lifetime, with his descendants playing a significant role in Irish and Scottish history. His influence can also be seen in the cultural and artistic achievements of the medieval period, including the development of Irish literature and music. The study of Selbach mac Ferchair's life and reign provides valuable insights into the complexities of Irish politics and the impact of leadership on a nation's development.
